summary: This is a code snippet configuration for a text editor's auto-completion feature. It defines a template called 'callout' that helps users quickly insert a formatted callout block (like a note or warning box) into a Markdown document by typing a short prefix and then filling in customizable parts.

explanations.3: The 'prefix' is the short text you type in your editor to trigger this template — in this case, typing 'quarto-callout' will offer this snippet as an auto-complete option.
explanations.5: This line shows a dropdown menu with choices — when the user inserts the template, they'll be prompted to pick one type from the list (note, tip, warning, etc.), and that choice gets filled into the template automatically.
explanations.6: The ${2:title} means the editor will jump to this spot second (after ${1}) and let the user type a title for the callout box.
explanations.7: The ${3:body} is where the user will type the actual content of the callout, and it's set to be filled in third after the type and title are chosen.
